text.p: Germany's Metallbank GmbH, formerly the in-house bank of the German industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG, on Wednesday reported a pre-tax profit of 21.2 million marks in the 1995/96 fiscal year.
Metallbank said that the year had started well in the first quarter and that it expected a successful year in 1996/97.
The bank said that the profit figure corresponds to a 19.3 percent return on equity, adding that its balance sheet total of 1.259 billion marks slightly exceeded the figure for the previous year.
Metallgesellschaft (MG) sold Metallbank to the private bank SchmidtBank KGaA on October 1 last year for an undisclosed sum, described at the time as a "good price".
Managing director of Metallbank, Lothar Mark, said that the bank's connection to MG was still very important to the group's operations, accounting for just under 50 percent of its pre-tax profits.
The bank still carries out operations for MG such as exchange and hedging transactions.

There was a contractual agreement between MG and Metallbank that the bank would retain its role as MG's main bank, but Metallbank said it would have to work harder on maintaining this business than previously.
MG occupied a very important role in Metallbank's private client business, with MG employees accounting for more than half of the bank's private clients.
The head of the family-owned SchmidtBank, Karl-Gerhard Schmidt, said that both banks in the merger would retain their individual indentities.
